name: Resmetirom
drug_class: Thyroid hormone receptor beta (THR-β) selective agonist
route_note: oral tablet once daily (80 or 100 mg by body weight)

discovery.by: Roche, then developed by VIA Pharmaceuticals / Madrigal
discovery.note: A liver-directed THR-β agonist designed to avoid THR-α-mediated effects on heart and bone. Year is the priority date of Roche's patent application on pyridazinone THR agonists (WO 2007/009913); the compound (MGL-3196) was first published in 2013–2014.

tagline: The first approved drug for MASH, a liver-targeted thyroid hormone mimic
summary: Resmetirom is an oral, liver-directed agonist of thyroid hormone receptor beta. In March 2024 it became the first drug approved for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH, formerly NASH) with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis, after the MAESTRO-NASH trial showed resolution of steatohepatitis and improvement of fibrosis.
mechanism: Thyroid hormone acting on THR-β in hepatocytes increases fatty-acid β-oxidation, mitochondrial biogenesis and cholesterol metabolism. Resmetirom is about 28-fold selective for THR-β over THR-α and is taken up preferentially into the liver by OATP1B1.

Liver fat falls, lipotoxicity and inflammation decrease, and LDL cholesterol, triglycerides and lipoprotein(a) decline. Avoiding THR-α activation is intended to spare the heart and bone from thyrotoxic effects.
uses: Non-cirrhotic MASH/NASH with moderate to advanced liver fibrosis (stages F2–F3), with diet and exercise

history.title: Licensed from Roche
history.detail: Madrigal's predecessor licenses the compound from Roche.

history.title: Phase 2 results
history.detail: A phase 2 trial shows significant reduction in liver fat at 12 weeks (Lancet 2019).

history.title: Topline phase 3 results
history.detail: In December 2022 Madrigal reports that MAESTRO-NASH met both liver-biopsy primary endpoints.

history.title: MAESTRO-NASH and FDA approval
history.detail: MAESTRO-NASH is published in NEJM; FDA grants accelerated approval to Rezdiffra on 14 March 2024 as the first MASH treatment.

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission grants conditional marketing authorisation for Rezdiffra in August 2025.

serious: interactions with statins and CYP2C8 inhibitors

facts: Rezdiffra was approved under the accelerated pathway, with continued approval contingent on outcome data from the MAESTRO-NASH OUTCOMES study.
